issue_context.title: [1.11 blocking] Overloading win+` doesn't work anymore
issue_context.body:
(discussed on Teams at length, but filing to make sure we're tracking)

Regressed in #10666.

Repro settings:

```json
{ "keys": "win+`", "command": { "action": "globalSummon", "monitor": "any" } }
{ "keys": "ctrl+shift+`", "command": { "action": "quakeMode" } }
```

The <kbd>win+\`</kbd> one will fail to override the <kbd>win+sc(43)</kbd> one in the defaults. When it gets time to `RegisterHotkey`, the one from the defaults will claim the hotkey first.

WIP over at [`dev/migrie/b/broken-globalsummon-overloading`](https://github.com/microsoft/terminal/compare/dev/migrie/b/broken-globalsummon-overloading). 

Also related to #10729. That might be the ultimate solution here, but if we can't get that for 1.11 then we'll need another workaround, or back out the `sc()` one.

review_comments: Seems like removing this `Copy()` call is unexpected? All the other `Copy()`s were left untouched - why this one?
Ah thank you for catching this! I've fixed it now.

I personally believe `assert` should be preferred over `FAIL_FAST_IF` for "soft-assertions".
What I mean is basically assertions, that if they break don't lead to dangerously incorrect behavior. This is the case here: If `_parents` did have more than 1 member, it would IMO be preferable to rather do the slightly wrong thing, as opposed to crashing the app and causing the user to loose their data.

I think @DHowett had some thoughts on removing `FAIL_FAST_IF`s from the codebase. Particularly regarding all of the ones in `Viewport` that caused a11y to shut down the whole app all the time (my fault). I don't recall what the resolution on that conversation was though.

That said, I'm ok with replacing `FAIL_FAST_IF`s with `assert`. It's compiled out of release builds, and if the condition isn't met in debug builds, it's treated like a `DebugBreak()` right?
Yeah `assert()` calls `_wassert()`, which creates the famous 3-button-dialog where you can choose what you want to do (debug-break, abort, or continue IIRC).

I don't know everywhere `IInheritable` is used, but it looks like at in `GlobalAppSettings`, `TerminalSettings`, and here in `ActionMap` it seems to enforced that there is at most one parent. If the ability to have multiple parents isn't actually used (I see some things with `Profile` but it is hard to tell if multiple direct parents is actually utilized compared to a chain of parents), wouldn't the better overall solution be to change IInheritable to have `std::optional<com_ptr<T>> _parent` instead?
@Rosefield Unfortunately profiles _can_ have multiple parents, which is why this is so weird and tricky 😕
